50991671.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to N-terminal His6-tagged KAT8 catalytic domain (125 to 458 residues) (unknown origin) expressed in Escherichia coli BL21(DE3) by isothermal titration calorimetry
50991671.references_previous: H. Wapenaar, P.E. van der Wouden, M.R. Groves, D. Rotili, A. Mai, F.J. Dekker, Enzyme kinetics and inhibition of histone acetyltransferase KAT8, Eur. J. Med. Chem. 105 (2015 Nov 13) 289–296.

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods: Isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC) experiments were performed using a MicroCal iTC200 (Malvern Instruments, Worcestershire, UK). The N-terminal His6-tagged KAT8 catalytic domain (125 to 458 residues) was expressed in Escherichia coli BL21(DE3) and purified as described previously [18]. The protein was dialyzed against 20 mM HEPES, pH 7.5, 100 mM NaCl, 1 mM DTT, 10% glycerol. The concentration of the protein was determined by Bradford assay. Compound 13 was dissolved in DMSO and diluted in the same buffer as the protein. The ITC experiments were performed at 25 °C with a stirring speed of 300 rpm. The protein (10 μM) was loaded into the sample cell, and the compound (1 mM) was loaded into the syringe. The compound was injected in 20 steps of 2 μL each, with a spacing of 120 s between injections. The first injection was 0.4 μL. The data were analyzed using Origin 7.0 software (OriginLab, Northampton, MA, USA) with a one-site binding model. The control experiment was performed by titrating the compound into buffer without protein. The heat of dilution was subtracted from the experimental data.

50991672.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to N-terminal His6-tagged KAT8 catalytic domain (125 to 458 residues) (unknown origin) expressed in Escherichia coli BL21(DE3) in presence of Ac-CoA by isothermal titration calorimetry
50991672.references_previous: H. Wapenaar, P.E. van der Wouden, M.R. Groves, D. Rotili, A. Mai, F.J. Dekker, Enzyme kinetics and inhibition of histone acetyltransferase KAT8, Eur. J. Med. Chem. 105 (2015 Nov 13) 289–296.

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods: Isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC) experiments were performed on a MicroCal iTC200 (Malvern Instruments, Worcestershire, UK) at 25 °C. The N-terminal His6-tagged KAT8 catalytic domain (125 to 458 residues) was expressed in Escherichia coli BL21(DE3) and purified as described previously [18]. The protein was dialyzed against 20 mM HEPES (pH 7.5), 100 mM NaCl, 1 mM DTT, 10% glycerol. The concentration of the protein was determined by Bradford assay. Compound 13 was dissolved in DMSO and diluted in the same buffer as the protein. The protein (10 μM) was loaded into the sample cell, and the compound (100 μM) was loaded into the syringe. The titration consisted of 20 injections of 2 μL each, with a spacing of 180 s between injections. The stirring speed was set to 300 rpm. A blank experiment was performed by titrating the compound into buffer without protein. The data were analyzed using Origin 7.0 software (OriginLab, Northampton, MA, USA) with a one-site binding model. The binding isotherm was fitted to the equation: Q = (n * ΔH * [I] * [P]) / (Kd + [I]) where Q is the heat released, n is the stoichiometry, ΔH is the enthalpy change, [I] is the concentration of the ligand, [P] is the concentration of the protein, and Kd is the dissociation constant. The dissociation constant (Kd) was calculated from the association constant (Ka) as Kd = 1/Ka. The binding affinity (Ka) was determined from the slope of the binding isotherm. The thermograms were corrected for the heat of dilution by subtracting the blank experiment. The data are presented as the mean ± standard deviation from two independent experiments.
original_paragraph.Figure 1 caption: C) The equilibrium dissociation constant (Kd) of 13 to KAT8 was determined using isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC). Compound 13 showed a Kd of 2.6 μM for KAT8. N = stoichiometry, K = association constant (1/Kd), Kd = equilibrium dissociation constant (1/K). D) The equilibrium dissociation constant (Kd) of 13 to KAT8 in the presence of Ac-CoA was determined using isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC). Compound 13 showed a Kd of 0.7 μM. N = stoichiometry, K = association constant (1/Kd), Kd = equilibrium dissociation constant (1/K).
original_paragraph.Results section: To further investigate this, binding studies of 13 to KAT8 were done using isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC). Compound 13 was titrated to KAT8 in the absence of Ac-CoA (the free enzyme) and the equilibrium dissociation constant (Kd) of 13 was determined (2.6 ± 0.7 μM, Fig. 1C, Fig. S10A). The stoichiometry of the interaction was close to one, suggesting that one molecule of 13 binds to one molecule of KAT8. Compound 13 was also titrated to KAT8 in the presence of Ac-CoA to generate a certain amount of the acetylated/Ac-CoA bound enzyme form. The binding data showed a Kd of 0.7 ± 0.06 μM (Fig. 1D, Fig. S10B). The Kd for Ac-CoA bound KAT8 is lower than for free KAT8, indicating that 13 binds with a higher affinity to the acetylated intermediate than to the free enzyme. These data suggest that compound 13 inhibits KAT8 by interacting both with the free enzyme form as well as with the Ac-CoA bound form, but has higher affinity for the acetylated intermediate.
